items.text: Cannabis is legal for adults 21 and over. The personal use amount is up to 1.5 ounces (about 42 g) of cannabis, 12 g of concentrate, or products holding up to 750 mg of THC (Criminal Law 5-101). Holding more, up to 2.5 ounces, 20 g of concentrate or 1,250 mg of THC, is a civil offence with a fine of up to US$250 (about A$355 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026); more than that is a crime. Smoking cannabis in a public place is a civil offence with a fine of up to US$50 for a first finding and US$150 for later ones (about A$71 and A$213) (Criminal Law 5-601).

laws.rule: A driver in Maryland may not use their hands to use a hand-held phone while the vehicle is moving, other than to start or end a call or turn the phone on or off (Transportation 21-1124.2). Emergency calls to 911, hospitals, ambulance, fire or police are allowed. Texting while driving is banned under a separate section (21-1124.1).
laws.penalty_signal: Up to US$75 for a first offence, US$125 for a second and US$175 for a third or later (about A$107, A$178 and A$249 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026); points only if it contributes to a crash

laws.rule: Maryland law bans wearing, carrying or transporting a handgun, openly or concealed, unless the person holds a Maryland permit (Criminal Law 4-203). Narrow exceptions cover carrying an unloaded handgun in an enclosed case to or from places such as a place of legal purchase or sale or a repair shop.
laws.penalty_signal: First offence: 30 days to 5 years in prison, a fine of US$250 to US$2,500 (about A$355 to A$3,551), or both
